target.role: STRANGE GAIT Track 2 after doctrine correction
target.position: after Inigo Kennedy — Marauder — Track 2 at end of ledger
target.purpose: re-evaluate doctrine-triggered exact candidates under transition, local-run and long-form DJ logic without imposing the retired same-room or fixed-Ground admission rule

source: Exact Spotify identity verified from a supplied public track ID or one unambiguous exact Spotify search match; BPM from the declared external source.

requestedIdentity.bpmSource: Previously verified repository resolver snapshot recorded in playlists/strange-gait/discoveries.md
requestedIdentity.discoverySource: playlists/strange-gait/discoveries.md — 2026-09-06 Vibe-first Run 1; same Flux Rope release as Marauder with official release description referencing rolling bass-heavy percussion and pads

proposedPlacements.position: after Inigo Kennedy — Marauder as Track 2

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Same-release context, exact 136 BPM identity and prior source-backed rhythmic description make this the strongest controlled continuation hypothesis, while the revised doctrine no longer requires proof of one identical felt-energy room.

evidence.attributedDescription: Prior official Flux Rope release evidence described rolling bass-heavy percussion and pads; this is attributed source language, not direct listening.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The listener reported that the prior four-track opening changed energy awkwardly track by track; that evidence applies to that failed sequence and requires deliberate flow here, but does not prove all vibe changes fail.
evidence.craftConvention: A same-release handoff is a useful controlled sequencing hypothesis, but not proof of perceived continuity.

proposedPlacements.position: after Inigo Kennedy — Marauder as Track 2

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Track-specific source evidence supports a body-first, restrained techno hypothesis that could make a deliberate move after Marauder; the 136→134 tempo change is measured context only, not the reason for admission.

evidence.attributedDescription: Moving Pressure source evidence previously recorded grounded physicality, hypnosis, murk and tension; this remains attributed evidence rather than model listening.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The failed prior opening warns against paper-only energy assumptions, but Cave was not part of that rejected sequence.
evidence.craftConvention: A modest tempo step and track-specific restraint framing make the placement worth exact reassessment without treating similarity as mandatory.

requestedIdentity.bpmSource: Previously verified repository resolver state recorded in playlists/strange-gait/discoveries.md and revisit.md
requestedIdentity.discoverySource: playlists/strange-gait/revisit.md — doctrine-triggered reopening because its prior trigger depended on a fixed Lock chapter and one-vibe protection; its polymetric/43EDO identity remains relevant to the volume lens

proposedPlacements.position: after Inigo Kennedy — Marauder as Track 2 as an intentionally conspicuous contrast

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Mystify strongly engages the structural-freedom selection lens and the global doctrine permits hard left turns, but its 16:31 duration and technical foregrounding make an opening placement a materially higher-risk hypothesis.

evidence.attributedDescription: Repository history identifies polymetric/43EDO structure as part of the track's documented identity; this is not a claim about perceived energy or exact mixability.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The listener disliked arbitrary-feeling energy resets in the prior opening, so any deliberate contrast here carries a higher burden of sequencing rationale.
evidence.craftConvention: A conspicuous early contrast can work in long-form sequencing, but it should not be used merely to advertise rhythmic novelty.
